current.text: He is projected as Brooklyn's backup center. Day'Ron Sharpe is the projected starter, and three of the five projected bench players are big men.
He signed with Brooklyn on a mutual option deal as veteran depth.
Brooklyn's center minutes are expected to be split between him, Sharpe and Danny Wolf.
Brooklyn may give more minutes to young players in the second half, including frontcourt players Noah Clowney and Josh Minott. That makes his late-season role uncertain.
Brooklyn is projected as one of the worst teams in the league, at about 28 wins.
Brooklyn has 16 back-to-backs, tied with Boston for the most in the league. For a season ending March 28, its playoff schedule is 3-4-3 games, with one back-to-back in the playoff weeks.

durable.text: He is an efficient, high-usage backup big who cannot handle 20 or more minutes a game.
